passages.context: The numbered Miscellaneous Notes. Note 2 refers calendar makers to Chapter II of the Universal Norms for diocesan and provincial calendars; note 3 quotes Universal Norms n. 15 on the Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary; note 4 records the 1992 Honolulu decree limiting Hawaii to two holy days of obligation; note 5 explains that Independence Day and Thanksgiving Day appear because they are inscribed in the Proper Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America; note 6 names the five ecclesiastical provinces that keep the Thursday Ascension and states that all others have transferred it to the following Sunday, records the 1998 notification on the Immaculate Heart, and applies the complementary norm to canon 1246 paragraph 2 to the Assumption falling on a Saturday.

passages.context: The daily entries that carry parenthetical Ordinary Time week numbers: the Monday after the Baptism of the Lord, which opens the First Week, and the entries in the days after Pentecost that name the week resumed after Easter Time and the weeks following it. Together with the pre-Lenten Sunday entries they fix the last week used before Lent and the first week resumed after Pentecost for this year.

passages.context: The front-matter tables headed Principal Celebrations of the Liturgical Year 2026, Cycles - Lectionary for Mass, and Liturgy of the Hours, together with the introductory paragraphs that describe how the cycles were applied. They give the two First Sundays of Advent bounding the year, Ash Wednesday, Easter, the Thursday Ascension, Pentecost, the Sunday Most Holy Body and Blood of Christ, the Sunday and weekday Lectionary letters with their exact intervals, and the volumes and week spans of the Liturgy of the Hours.

work.author: United States Conference of Catholic Bishops, Secretariat of Divine Worship
work.description: The annual calendar published by the Secretariat of Divine Worship for the dioceses of the United States of America, resolving the General Roman Calendar and the Proper Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America for one liturgical year. Each civil year is a distinct edition. It is a competent territorial witness to a year's resolution, not the promulgating source of the recurring proper calendar.
work.title: Liturgical Calendar for the Dioceses of the United States of America
